chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The jurists and the wise, when they wrote to one another, would write with three things, and there was no fourth with them: One whose concern was the Hereafter, Allah would suffice him from the concern of the world; and one who improved his interior, Allah would improve his exterior; and one who improved what was between him and Allah, Allah would improve what was between him and the people.'

key_terms.أَمِیرُ الْمُؤْمِنِینَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (a.s.)
key_terms.الْحُکَمَاءُ: The wise, those possessing wisdom and insight
key_terms.سَرِیرَتَهُ: His interior, inner self or secret state
key_terms.عَلَانِیَتَهُ: His exterior, public state or visible conduct

ai.seo_question: What were the three main themes in the letters of early Shia jurists and wise men?
ai.summary: This hadith from Thawab al-Amal highlights the tripartite spiritual methodology of the early Shia jurists, linking inner sincerity (sirrah) to outward integrity (alaniyah) and divine-human relations to social harmony. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the unity of worship and ethics, where rectifying one's relationship with Allah directly influences one's conduct with creation, a concept deeply rooted in the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt.
